source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 102: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: pin model, calculator version, precision semantics, workload, load, and correctness adjudicator; measure rather than invent platform facts. Define unnecessary as a call where no-tool answers correctly at stated precision; justified calls cover error-prone/large arithmetic, conversions, uncertainty, missing intermediates, or verification. Ask or abstain on ambiguous operands, units, rounding, or precision. Use a typed stop/no-tool gate recording task class, difficulty, precision, and rationale; require expected correctness gain to exceed measured latency/cost, reject duplicates, and bound calls/retries. Measure unnecessary-call rate, justified-use recall, tool success/error/timeout/wrong-result, final correctness, abstentions, trajectory length, calls, retries, recovery, tool/end-to-end latency in milliseconds, and token/currency cost. Redact or hash private expressions and enforce authorization, retention, and access controls. Reward correct concise no-tool answers only with correctness gates, penalizing needless or unsafe tool use. Hypothesis: on a locked stratified held-out set, intervention lowers unnecessary calls and median/p95 latency/cost while correctness stays within a predeclared non-inferiority margin and justified-use recall does not fall. Randomize paired tasks, keep tuning/evaluation disjoint, report confidence intervals and slices, and independently adjudicate correctness. Test no-tool, tool-required, ambiguity/precision, malformed/adversarial output, wrong result, timeout, duplicate/retry-loop, and unavailable-tool cases. Canary and roll back on correctness, recall, recovery, tail-latency, privacy, authorization, or safety threshold breaches. Evidence is required before treating this provisional result as authoritative.
